mainTopic: The ציץ and gentile offerings; when טומאה and נותר liability apply to items without מתירין
overview: The amud opens with the end of a ברייתא about blood that became טמא and was then sprinkled. The ציץ makes an individual's offering acceptable only if this was done by mistake. A community's offering is accepted either way, and a gentile's offering is never accepted. The חכמים ask whether this can fit רבי יוסי, who is strict about gentile offerings. רב פפא answers from the word 'for them,' but רב הונא בריה דרב נתן challenges that reading, and רב אשי instead explains that גוים are not part of the ציץ's הרצאה. A new משנה then teaches that items with no פיגול liability still carry נותר and טומאה liability, except blood. רבי שמעון limits the טומאה liability to things normally eaten. A ברייתא shows from a פסוק that טומאה liability covers every consecrated item, and that it starts once the item is fit to be offered. The גמרא then looks for the source of the same rule for נותר. It weighs learning it from טומאה against learning it from פיגול, and finally turns to a teaching of לוי, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: When impure blood is still accepted: individual, community, and gentile offerings
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its rule. For an individual, blood sprinkled in טומאה on purpose is not accepted. For the ציבור, it is accepted whether by mistake or on purpose. For גוים, it is not accepted in either case.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did it on purpose, it was not accepted. When does this apply? To an individual's offering. But for a community offering, whether by mistake or on purpose, it was accepted. And for gentiles' offerings, whether by mistake or on purpose, it was not accepted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא that sorts out when an offering whose blood was sprinkled while impure still counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three groups and three outcomes. For a יחיד, only a שוגג sprinkling is accepted. For the ציבור, even a מזיד sprinkling is accepted. For גוים, nothing is accepted. This last rule about גוים is what the rest of the סוגיא will question.

keyTerms.meaning: It was accepted, meaning the offering counts
On purpose, knowingly
By mistake, without knowing
An individual's private offering
The community; a communal offering
Gentiles (here, offerings brought by non-Jews)

phrases.english: If on purpose, it was not accepted.
phrases.notes: This continues the ברייתא's earlier line: if impure blood was sprinkled by mistake, the offering was accepted.

phrases.english: When are these words said? For an individual;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּצִיבּוּר, בֵּין בְּשׁוֹגֵג בֵּין בְּמֵזִיד – הוּרְצָה.
phrases.english: but for the community, whether by mistake or on purpose, it was accepted.

phrases.aramaic: וּבְגוֹיִם, בֵּין בְּשׁוֹגֵג וּבֵין בְּמֵזִיד – לֹא הוּרְצָה.
phrases.english: And for gentiles, whether by mistake or on purpose, it was not accepted.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Impure blood sprinkled for an individual is accepted only if sprinkled by mistake. For the community it is accepted either way. For gentiles it is never accepted.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that gentile offerings are never accepted is the trigger for the question about רבי יוסי that follows.

steps.title: The ברייתא seems not to match רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים point out to רב פפא that the ברייתא's rule excluding גוים seems to go against רבי יוסי, who says he treats gentile offerings strictly in all these laws.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages said before רב פפא: Whose view is this? It is not like רבי יוסי. Because if it were רבי יוסי, doesn't he say: 'In all of them I see reason to be strict'?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים ask whose opinion the ברייתא follows. They point out that it seems to clash with רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי treats קדשים of גוים like Jewish קדשים in all these laws, and that is the strict approach. So he should also let the ציץ work for a gentile offering. The ברייתא says it does not, so it seems to go against him.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom? Whose view is this?
They said it before him
To be strict

phrases.english: The Sages said it before Rav Pappa:
Whose view is this? Not like Rabbi Yosei;
because if it were Rabbi Yosei, doesn't he say:
'In all of them I see reason to be strict!'
phrases.notes: He means gentile offerings: in all these laws he treats them strictly, just like Jewish offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whose opinion the ברייתא in step 1 follows
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule that gentile offerings are never accepted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי treats gentile קדשים exactly like Jewish ones, so under his view the ציץ should work for them too.

steps.title: רב פפא: the ציץ is different because the פסוק says 'for them'
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the ברייתא can fit רבי יוסי. The ציץ is a special case, because its פסוק says 'for them,' which means Jews and not גוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to them: You can even say it follows רבי יוסי. It is different there, because the verse says 'for them': for them, and not for gentiles.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא defends the ברייתא. He shows that it can match רבי יוסי after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's general strictness about gentile offerings stays in place. The ציץ is simply a special exception, because the Torah limits it with the word 'לָהֶם.' So רבי יוסי can be strict elsewhere and still agree that the ציץ does not help a gentile's offering.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say
It is different there
The verse
The כהן גדול's golden headplate, which makes offerings with certain impurity acceptable

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to them:
You can even say it is Rabbi Yosei,
it is different there, because the verse says:
'for them': for them, and not for gentiles.
phrases.notes: שמות 28:38, the פסוק about the ציץ.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, שָׁאנֵי הָתָם דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Exception from a פסוק: a specific verse limits the ציץ to Jews
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי's strictness means the ציץ should work for gentile offerings too
steps.terutzMaskana: Even רבי יוסי agrees that the ציץ works only for Jews, because of the word 'לָהֶם'
steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא is not saying רבי יוסי changed his mind about gentile offerings. He is saying the ציץ is a separate case with its own limiting פסוק.

steps.title: רב הונא בריה דרב נתן: then 'which they consecrate' should also leave out gentiles
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב נתן challenges רב פפא. If 'for them' excludes גוים, then the פסוק about טומאה, 'which they consecrate,' should also exclude גוים. But רבי יוסי includes them there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב נתן said to רב פפא: If so, then the verse 'which they consecrate', should we also say: they, and not gentiles?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא's way of reading the פסוק is being challenged. The challenge uses a similar word in another פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about eating קדשים in טומאה also uses a word meaning 'they.' If רב פפא's reasoning is right, that verse should exclude gentile offerings too. But רבי יוסי clearly holds that gentile קדשים do carry the טומאה prohibition, so רב פפא's method seems to prove too much.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so (now that you said this)
They consecrate (set aside as holy)
So too? Would you say the same here?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן לְרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Natan said to Rav Pappa:
But if so,
'which they consecrate':
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:2

phrases.english: so too, 'they' and not gentiles?!
phrases.notes: That can't be, because רבי יוסי holds this prohibition does apply to gentile offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's answer in step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's reading that 'לָהֶם' excludes gentiles
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A similar word in ויקרא 22:2 would then exclude gentiles from the טומאה prohibition. That goes against רבי יוסי, who includes them.

steps.title: רב אשי: The exclusion comes from the word 'acceptance'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי drops רב פפא's reading of 'for them.' He says גוים are excluded because the ציץ works through הרצאה, and גוים are not subject to הרצאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: The פסוק says 'to be accepted for them,' and gentiles are not people who receive acceptance.
steps.whatsHappening: Because רב הונא בריה דרב נתן's challenge knocked down רב פפא's answer, רב אשי offers a different reason why the ברייתא can still fit רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא based the exclusion on the word 'להם,' and that was attacked, because the טומאה פסוק also says 'they' and still includes גוים. רב אשי moves the focus to the word 'לרצון.' The ציץ's power is to make an offering acceptable, and גוים are simply not in that system. So the exclusion comes from the nature of the ציץ, not from a general word like 'them.' This means the טומאה פסוק is not affected.

keyTerms.meaning: For acceptance, meaning that the offering is accepted for the owner
The process of making an offering acceptable, which is what the ציץ does
People who are part of the acceptance system
Rather. It signals that the earlier answer is being dropped

steps.whatToRemember: The final answer is רב אשי's. The ציץ does not help a gentile's offering because the ציץ works through הרצאה, and גוים are not subject to הרצאה. That is why the ברייתא can still fit רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
The verse says: "to be accepted for them"
phrases.notes: שמות 28:38. This is the פסוק about the ציץ. This time the focus is on the word 'acceptance,' not on 'them.'

phrases.english: and gentiles are not subject to acceptance.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It replaces רב פפא's answer (Step 3) after that answer was challenged in Step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New source reading: a different word in the same פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The exclusion of גוים comes from 'להם,' and that would wrongly exclude them from the טומאה law too.
steps.terutzMaskana: The exclusion comes from 'לרצון.' גוים are not subject to the ציץ's הרצאה, so the טומאה law is not affected.

steps.title: משנה: Liability for נותר and טומאה even without פיגול
steps.stepSummary: Items that carry no פיגול liability still carry liability for נותר and טומאה, except for blood. רבי שמעון says טומאה liability applies only to food that is normally eaten, so it excludes wood, לבונה, and קטורת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Items for which one is not liable because of פיגול are still liable because of נותר and because of eating while טמא, except for the blood. רבי שמעון makes one liable only for things normally eaten. But for wood, frankincense, and incense, there is no טומאה liability.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that the items that were exempt from פיגול are still covered by the laws of נותר and טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous משנה listed items that cannot become פיגול. This משנה teaches that being exempt from פיגול does not exempt them from נותר or טומאה. Blood is the one exception. רבי שמעון narrows the טומאה rule to things people normally eat, so wood, לבונה, and קטורת are not included.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering made invalid by a wrong intention about its time. Eating it carries כרת
Sacrificial meat left over past its time limit
Ritually impure. Here it refers to eating קדשים while impure
Frankincense
The incense burned in the בית המקדש

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that 'no פיגול liability' means 'no liability at all.' The משנה says these items still carry נותר and טומאה liability. Blood is the only exception, and רבי שמעון adds his own limit.

phrases.english: Mishnah

phrases.aramaic: דְּבָרִים שֶׁאֵין חַיָּיבִים עֲלֵיהֶם מִשּׁוּם פִּיגּוּל,
phrases.english: Items for which one is not liable because of piggul,
one is liable for them because of notar
and because of eating while impure;
except for the blood.
Rabbi Shimon holds one liable
for an item that people normally eat,
but the wood, the frankincense, and the incense,
one is not liable for them because of impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ דְּבָרִים שֶׁאֵין חַיָּיבִים עֲלֵיהֶם מִשּׁוּם פִּיגּוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה. It starts a new topic after the ציץ discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Items exempt from פיגול still carry נותר and טומאה liability, except blood. רבי שמעון limits טומאה liability to items that are normally eaten.

steps.title: ברייתא: Maybe impurity liability needs permitting factors
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא raises a possible idea: maybe טומאה liability applies only to items that have מתירין, whether for a person or for the altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: One might think that a person is liable for טומאה only on an item that has permitting factors, whether for a person or for the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא that suggests a possible limit on the טומאה law. It is setting up an argument that will then be tested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'יכול' means 'you might have thought.' It introduces an idea that the ברייתא rejects in step 10. The idea is that טומאה liability, like פיגול liability, should depend on the item having a מתיר. If it worked that way, items with no מתיר would carry no טומאה liability, and that would go against the משנה's broad rule.

keyTerms.meaning: One might think. It introduces an idea that will be tested
Permitting factors: the service, like sprinkling blood, that makes an item permitted

phrases.english: Gemara
The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל לֹא יְהוּ חַיָּיבִין מִשּׁוּם טוּמְאָה
phrases.english: One might think one should not be liable because of impurity

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא עַל דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ מַתִּירִין –
phrases.english: except for an item that has permitting factors,
phrases.notes: A 'מתיר' is the service that allows the item to be eaten or burned, like sprinkling the blood.

phrases.english: whether for a person or for the altar?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: יָכוֹל לֹא יְהוּ חַיָּיבִין מִשּׁוּם טוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that deals with the scope of the משנה's טומאה liability.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A possible idea: טומאה liability might apply only to items that have מתירין.

steps.title: A קל וחומר from פיגול begins
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא supports its idea with a קל וחומר. פיגול is stricter in several ways, and still it applies only to items that have מתירין. So the softer law of טומאה should be limited the same way. The argument is finished in step 9.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is logical. פיגול has a fixed חטאת, needs only one awareness, and has no permitted exception. Yet one is liable for it only on items that have permitting factors, whether for a person or for the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא starts building a קל וחומר to back up the idea from Step 7. It lays out the strict side, פיגול, and the comparison to טומאה is still to come.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פיגול is shown as stricter than טומאה in three ways. It carries a fixed חטאת, not a sliding-scale offering. It needs only one awareness. And it has no case where it is ever permitted. Even so, פיגול applies only to items with מתירין. The point being prepared is that טומאה, which is softer, should certainly be limited the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is logical. It introduces a reasoned proof such as a קל וחומר
Just as. It opens the strict side of a קל וחומר
A fixed חטאת, the same for everyone, unlike a sliding-scale offering
One awareness: knowing about the sin only afterward is enough
No exception to its prohibition is ever permitted

steps.confusionAlert: This step stops in the middle of the קל וחומר. The 'so too טומאה' conclusion comes in step 9, and the ברייתא rejects the whole argument with a פסוק in step 10.

phrases.english: And it is logical:
Just as piggul,
which carries a fixed offering
phrases.notes: He means a fixed חטאת, the same for rich and poor, unlike the sliding-scale offering for טומאה.

phrases.english: and requires only one awareness
and has no permitted exception to its general rule,
one is not liable for it

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא עַל דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ מַתִּירִין,
phrases.english: except for an item that has permitting factors,
whether for a person or for the altar;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It gives the logical support (a קל וחומר) for the idea raised in Step 7.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that טומאה liability applies only to items with מתירין
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from פיגול, which is stricter yet still limited to items with מתירין

steps.title: טומאה is the softer law, so it should be limited too
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its קל וחומר. טומאה is more lenient than פיגול in three ways, so it should surely apply only to items that have מתירין.
steps.simpleTranslation: טומאה only brings a sliding-scale offering. It needs two moments of awareness. It also has exceptions where it is allowed. So isn't it logical that a person is liable only for an item that has permitting factors, whether for a person or for the altar?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes the קל וחומר it began in the last step. It lists three ways that טומאה is softer than פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פיגול is the stricter law, and it still applies only to items with מתירין. טומאה is softer in three ways: it only needs a קרבן עולה ויורד, it needs two ידיעות, and it is allowed for the community. So the logic says טומאה should be limited to items with מתירין as well.

keyTerms.meaning: A sliding-scale offering that changes with what the sinner can afford
Two moments of awareness: he knew, then forgot, then found out again
Has exceptions from its general rule (here, communal offerings may be brought in טומאה)
Isn't it logical? This is the phrase that closes a קל וחומר

steps.confusionAlert: This is only a 'maybe' (a יכול). The ברייתא is about to reject it in the next step, so do not take it as the final הלכה.

phrases.english: Impurity, which is with a sliding-scale offering
phrases.notes: He means the sin of eating holy food while טמא only needs a sliding-scale offering, which is softer than a set חטאת.

phrases.english: and requires two awarenesses
and was permitted from its general rule –
is it not logical that one is not liable

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא עַל דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ מַתִּירִין,
phrases.english: except for an item that has permitting factors,
whether for a person or for the altar?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁאֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא עַל דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ מַתִּירִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the קל וחומר that step 8 began
steps.raayaObject: The idea that טומאה liability is limited to items with מתירין
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from פיגול, which is stricter and yet limited to items with מתירין

steps.title: The verse includes everything that is consecrated
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'אשר הם מקדישים לי' overrides the קל וחומר. טומאה liability applies to anything that was consecrated.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is why the verse says: 'which they consecrate to Me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא throws out the קל וחומר by pointing to a פסוק that includes every holy item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'which they consecrate to Me' are broad. They cover anything consecrated, even items with no מתירין such as wood or לבונה. A clear פסוק beats a קל וחומר, so the limit the logic suggested does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore the verse teaches: this brings a פסוק to settle the question
They consecrate (make holy)

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why טומאה liability is broader than פיגול liability. That matches step 6, where items with no פיגול liability still carry טומאה liability.

phrases.english: The verse states: "which they consecrate to Me."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:2

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: אֲשֶׁר הֵם מַקְדִּישִׁים לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר from step 9 using a פסוק
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proposed limit of טומאה to items with מתירין
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A clear פסוק includes every consecrated item, so the logic cannot limit it

steps.title: Is one liable right away?
steps.stepSummary: Now that every holy item is included, the ברייתא asks whether liability begins the moment the item is consecrated.
steps.simpleTranslation: Might one think liability starts immediately?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a new question about timing. It is setting up the next move, where a פסוק will answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last step settled which items are included. This step asks a different question: from when? Maybe someone who is טמא and eats the item is liable as soon as it becomes holy.

keyTerms.meaning: One might think: introduces a possible idea that will be checked
Immediately, right away

phrases.english: One might think, immediately?
phrases.notes: He means liability for eating it while טמא, right from the moment it becomes holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from which items are included to when liability begins
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether טומאה liability begins as soon as an item is consecrated

steps.title: The verse says 'approaches'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers from the word 'יקרב'. Liability does not begin immediately.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is why the verse says: 'approaches.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the timing question with the word 'יקרב' in the פסוק. It has not yet explained how the word teaches this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'יקרב' is the source that liability is not immediate. The next steps explain how it teaches this, because read literally it does not seem to fit.

keyTerms.meaning: Approaches. It shares a root with הַקְרָבָה, offering on the altar

phrases.english: The verse states: "approaches."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:3

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Liability is not immediate, as the word 'יקרב' shows

steps.title: Approaching alone carries no liability
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר points out that the word cannot mean simply 'approaching,' because touching holy food does not make a person liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Is there anyone who just touches holy food and is liable?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר shows that 'approaches' cannot be read literally. He sets up a different reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taken literally, 'approaches' would mean a טמא person is liable just for coming near or touching holy food. But the only liability is for eating it. So the word must be hinting at something else.

keyTerms.meaning: One who touches
But is it so? Opens a surprised question

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
But is there one who touches who is liable?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the plain reading of the word quoted in step 12
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Touching holy food carries no liability, so the literal meaning does not work

steps.title: Approaches means fit to be offered
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר reads 'יקרב' as a hint to הקרבה. The פסוק is talking about meat that has become fit to be offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: So why does the verse say 'approaches'? The verse is talking about meat that has become fit to be offered.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives the true meaning of 'יקרב'. It tells us when liability begins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'יקרב' has the same root as הקרבה, offering on the altar. So the פסוק is talking about an item that has reached the stage where it is fit to be offered. Before that, a טמא person who eats it is not liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Became fit, ready
To be offered on the altar
The verse is speaking about

phrases.english: Rather, why does the verse state "approaches"?
About meat that has become fit to be offered
phrases.notes: The word 'meat' in square brackets is part of the corrected wording; some versions don't have it.

phrases.english: the verse is speaking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אלעזר's own question from step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads the word based on its root
steps.terutzMaskana: 'יקרב' hints to הקרבה, so the item must be fit to be offered

steps.title: When liability starts for each kind of item
steps.stepSummary: There are two cases. If an item has מתירין, liability starts once the מתירין are offered. If it has none, liability starts once it is made holy in a כלי שרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does this work? If an item has permitting factors, liability starts once its permitting factors are offered. If it has no permitting factors, liability starts once it is made holy in a service vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא sums up exactly when each type of item becomes 'fit to be offered.' That is the moment טומאה liability begins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For an animal, the point of being fit is when its מתירין, such as the blood, are offered. For items with no מתירין, such as לבונה, it is the moment they become holy in a כלי שרת. Before these points, a טמא person who eats the item is not liable.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? Opens a detailed explanation
From when it is made holy in a service vessel
A Temple service vessel

steps.whatToRemember: טומאה liability covers every consecrated item, not just those with מתירין. But it starts only once the item is fit to be offered. With מתירין, that is after they are offered. Without מתירין, that is after the item is made holy in a כלי.

phrases.english: How so?
If it has permitting factors –
from when the permitting factors are offered,
if it has no permitting factors –
from when it is made holy in a vessel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out in practice the rule from step 14
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: With מתירין, טומאה liability begins once they are offered. Without מתירין, it begins once the item is made holy in a כלי שרת.

steps.title: What about leftover meat?
steps.stepSummary: The rule for טומאה is settled. The גמרא now asks where we learn the same rule for נותר.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have found the source for טומאה. From where do we learn the rule for נותר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It has proven the rule for טומאה, and now asks how we know the same rule applies to נותר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא showed that someone who eats holy food while טמא is liable even when the item has no מתירין. The question is whether נותר works the same way. The verse about נותר does not say this outright, so a source is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: We have found (a source)
Sacrificial meat left over past its time limit, which is forbidden to eat
From where do we know?
The parts of the service, such as sprinkling the blood, that make an offering permitted

phrases.english: We have found it for impurity; for leftover meat, from where do we know?
phrases.notes: 'It' means the rule from the last step: liability applies even to an item that has no מתירין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the rule just set for טומאה to a second איסור, נותר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that נותר also applies to items that have no מתירין.

steps.title: Learning leftover meat from impurity
steps.stepSummary: נותר is learned from טומאה through a גזירה שוה on the word 'חילול'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is learned from 'profaning' and 'profaning,' from impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a גזירה שוה. The word 'חילול' appears in the verse about נותר and also in the verse about טומאה, so the two share the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because of this shared word, whatever is true of טומאה is also true of נותר. טומאה applies even without מתירין, so נותר does too.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning a law from a word that appears in two different places in the תורה
Profaning; treating something holy as ordinary

phrases.english: It comes from 'profaning'–'profaning' from impurity.
phrases.notes: The two verses are ויקרא 19:8 for נותר and ויקרא 22:2 for טומאה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה of 'חילול' connects נותר to טומאה, so נותר also applies without מתירין.

steps.title: Maybe compare it to פיגול instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: why not learn נותר from פיגול through the shared word 'עון'?
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us learn it from 'iniquity' and 'iniquity,' from פיגול!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a different word link. The word 'עון' appears in the verse about נותר and also in the verse about פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פיגול applies only to items that have מתירין. If נותר is learned from פיגול, the result is the opposite of step 17: נותר would not apply to items without מתירין. So two word links pull toward two different answers.

keyTerms.meaning: Iniquity, sin
An offering ruined by a wrong intention about when it will be eaten
But let us learn (from here instead)!

phrases.english: But let it be learned from 'iniquity'–'iniquity' from piggul!
phrases.notes: The verses are ויקרא 7:18 for פיגול and ויקרא 19:8 for נותר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source given in step 17 by offering a competing word link.
steps.kashyaTarget: The גזירה שוה from טומאה in step 17.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A competing גזירה שוה with פיגול exists and would lead to the opposite result, so why prefer טומאה?

steps.title: Impurity is the closer match
steps.stepSummary: It makes more sense to learn נותר from טומאה because the two share three features, remembered by the sign גז"ל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is more reasonable to learn it from impurity, since there is the sign גז"ל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that טומאה is the better source, because נותר and טומאה are alike in three ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three ways are: (ג) גוף, both are a problem in the meat itself, while פיגול comes from a person's wrong thought. (ז) זריקה, neither depends on the sprinkling of the blood, while פיגול does. (ל) חילול, the תורה uses the word 'profaning' for both.

keyTerms.meaning: It is more reasonable
A memory sign, a short code to help remember a list
The body of the offering itself
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח

phrases.english: It is more reasonable that he should learn it from impurity,
since there is the sign: גז"ל.
phrases.notes: Each letter is one shared feature: גוף (the meat itself), זריקה (sprinkling), and חילול (profaning).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends step 17 against the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Measuring which case is more similar, to decide between two competing גזירות שוות.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word link with פיגול is just as strong as the one with טומאה.
steps.terutzMaskana: טומאה is the closer match because it shares three features with נותר.

steps.title: No, פיגול shares even more features
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: נותר shares five features with פיגול, which is more than the three it shares with טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, he should learn it from פיגול, since: no permitted exception, the ציץ, pure, time, offered. And these are more numerous!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the argument around. It lists five ways נותר is like פיגול and points out that five is more than three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here is how נותר and פיגול match, and טומאה does not. Neither has a permitted exception. The ציץ does not atone for them. Both apply to pure meat. Both depend on time. Both are a problem in the offering, not in the person doing the service. So by counting features, פיגול now looks like the better source, and this knocks down the answer of step 19.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary
The כהן גדול's gold forehead plate, which atones for some problems with offerings
Was permitted (has an exception)
They are more numerous

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the final answer. The גמרא is only showing that counting features seems to favor פיגול. The next step settles the question by dropping this comparison and bringing a different source, the teaching of לוי.

phrases.english: On the contrary, he should learn it from piggul –

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן הוּתַּר, צִיץ, טָהוֹר, בִּזְמַן, קָרֵב;
phrases.english: since: permitted, frontplate, pure, in time, offered;
phrases.notes: These are five short code words for five shared features. Each one is explained in the deeper analysis above.

phrases.english: And these are more numerous!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 19 by bringing a longer list of shared features with פיגול.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 19 that טומאה is the closer match.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If we choose by counting shared features, פיגול has five and טומאה has only three, so נותר should follow פיגול.

steps.title: Dropping the comparison and turning to לוי's teaching
steps.stepSummary: Because the challenge from פיגול cannot easily be answered, the גמרא drops the גזירה שוה from טומאה. It says the rule for נותר comes instead from a teaching of לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the rule for נותר is learned from what לוי taught.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on learning נותר from טומאה through the word 'חילול'. It announces a different source, a ברייתא of לוי. This line is a setup, and the actual teaching comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אלא' (rather) tells us the earlier answer is being set aside. The question of which case is more similar, טומאה or פיגול, no longer needs to be settled. The גמרא will show the rule for נותר in a different way.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. A signal that the גמרא is dropping the previous answer and offering a new one.
From what [someone] taught, meaning a ברייתא is about to be quoted.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא answered the challenge about the five shared features with פיגול. It did not answer it. It stepped around it by finding a completely different source.

phrases.english: Rather, [it is learned] from what Levi taught.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the challenge in step 20 by dropping the גזירה שוה from טומאה and switching to a new source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replacing the source: the challenged derivation is dropped and a different source is brought in.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: נותר was learned from טומאה through the shared word 'חילול', and that left the door open to learning it from פיגול instead.
steps.terutzMaskana: נותר is learned from לוי's ברייתא, so there is no need to choose between טומאה and פיגול.

steps.title: לוי's teaching: the verse also covers disqualification by time
steps.stepSummary: לוי's ברייתא asks how we know the verse about eating holy food in טומאה is also talking about food that became disqualified by time. It answers from the פסוק 'ולא יחללו את קדשי בני ישראל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As לוי taught: How do we know that the verse is also talking about a disqualification caused by time? The verse says: 'And they shall not profane the holy things of the children of Israel.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes לוי's ברייתא. It asks how we know the verse also includes something disqualified because its time ran out, and it begins the answer with a פסוק. The ברייתא continues after this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse being discussed is about eating holy food while impure. לוי wants to show it also covers פסול זמן, a disqualification caused by time, which includes נותר. To do this he brings a second פסוק that uses the word 'profane' (יחללו).

keyTerms.meaning: From where [do we know]? The standard way of asking for a source.
A disqualification caused by time, when a קרבן becomes unfit because its time limit passed. נותר is this kind of case.
The verse is speaking [about this case].
The verse teaches. This introduces the פסוק that serves as the source.
They shall profane, from the root חילול.

steps.whyThisMatters: This makes נותר part of the same verse that gives the rule for טומאה. That gives נותר its source directly, without the disputed comparison.

phrases.english: As Levi taught:

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאַף בִּפְסוּל זְמַן הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר?
phrases.english: From where [do we know] that the verse is speaking even of a disqualification caused by time?
phrases.notes: 'The verse' here is the one about eating holy food while impure (ויקרא 22:2).

phrases.english: The verse states:
"And they shall not profane the holy things of the children of Israel" –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:15. The dash means לוי's teaching keeps going.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנֵי לֵוִי מִנַּיִן שֶׁאַף בִּפְסוּל זְמַן הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the ברייתא of לוי that step 21 announced.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The verse about eating holy food in טומאה also includes a disqualification caused by time. This is shown from 'ולא יחללו את קדשי בני ישראל'.
